intro: Nepal rises from steamy lowlands to the roof of the world in just about 150 km, with eight of the world's ten highest mountains.

chapters.title: The Himalayas
text: Mount Everest, called Sagarmatha in Nepali, is the highest point on Earth at 8,849 m, on the border with China. Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu and Annapurna are also in or on the edge of Nepal.
The Himalayas are still rising as India pushes into Asia, which also causes earthquakes.

chapters.title: Hills and the Terai
text: The middle hills hold Kathmandu and most towns. The Terai, flat lowlands along India, has rice fields and jungles where tigers and one-horned rhinos live in Chitwan National Park.

keyTerms.meaning: A giant slab of the Earth's crust.
